hyperparameter_selection: fresh_full_dataset_optuna: one new Optuna study of 100 trials was run on the complete development dataset (15 subjects, 9654 rows), using the same search space (config.XGB_SEARCH_SPACE) and the same composite objective as every LOSO fold's nested-CV search (loso_runner.run_optuna_study). The returned hyperparameters are this study's own best trial (composite=0.8650, precision=0.900, recall=0.865, f1=0.882) -- an actual combination this study evaluated via its own internal GroupKFold inner CV, never a selection among the 15 LOSO folds' best_params and never an elementwise per-key median/mode recombination across them. NOTE: LOSO (the loop that just finished) is used exclusively for unbiased performance estimation -- see outputs/reports/overall_metrics.json and per_subject_metrics.csv, both untouched by this study. This deployment model is a separate, later artifact retrained on the complete dataset with its own fresh optimization, and carries no unbiased performance estimate of its own.
decision_threshold_source: best_trial.user_attrs['threshold'] from the same fresh, full-dataset Optuna study (loso_runner.run_final_optuna_study) that selected final_params above -- the median of that trial's own inner-CV GroupKFold fold thresholds over the complete development dataset, computed via metrics.find_threshold_recall_at_precision, identical in method to every LOSO fold's own threshold

preprocessing.description: preprocessing.per_subject_baseline_normalize applied upstream of this model (in preprocessing.full_prepare, before LOSO/final-model training even begins), using each subject's own baseline-condition rows only. At inference time on a NEW subject with no prior baseline recording, this step cannot be replicated exactly -- see the 'How to load and use' notes for the practical implication.

generalization_estimate_caveat: This model was trained on ALL available subjects, so it has no unbiased held-out evaluation of its own. Use the LOSO results in outputs/reports/overall_metrics.json and per_subject_metrics.csv -- produced by evaluating this SAME hyperparameter configuration across 15 held-out subjects -- as the expected real-world performance estimate for this deployment model.
